'''Demicks Lake Pipeline''' is a cancelled natural gas pipeline in the United States.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Aug2018.xlsx|title=eia.gov|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline was proposed to run from North Dakota to Demicks Lake gas plant, near Keene, McKenzie County, North Dakota.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-05/june-infrastructure.pdf|title=ferc.gov|website=ferc.gov|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>

==Project Details==
===Main Line===
*'''Owner: '''WBI Energy Transmission Inc<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Aug2018.xlsx|title=eia.gov|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-05/june-infrastructure.pdf|title=ferc.gov|website=ferc.gov|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>
*'''Capacity: '''222 MMcf/d<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Aug2018.xlsx|title=eia.gov|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>
*'''Length: '''22 mi<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Aug2018.xlsx|title=eia.gov|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>
*'''Diameter: '''24 in<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Aug2018.xlsx|title=eia.gov|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>
*'''Status: '''Cancelled<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Aug2018.xlsx|title=eia.gov|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>
